title: M156 · Scout spike, half C (findings in; a 30-minute PC check settles the route)
summary: Half C is on mission/M156-scout-replay-spike (pushed). docs/scout-findings.md has the facts table, go/no-go per signal, the route, the portal question as sent, the licence note and the privacy rules. Top-down (route B) is GO: median error 127.8 world units, 82 % of champion health bars found. Minimap (route A) is PARTIAL: median 172.3, detection 0.78, longest gap 116 s. Most of that error is one identity bug (K: Pyke, Jax and Zed locked onto fixed background spots), fixed since; on 57 saved frames the fixed tracker drops the error from 519 to 162. Wards after fix E: blue 0.89/0.89, red 0.80/0.57. They stay NO-GO until you re-mark the hand check, because the v2 file carries your v1 verdicts. Recalls: precision 0.86, recall only 0.09; the track is rarely at the fountain while you shop. Recording runs at about 10× real time but only once per Windows sign-in. Twelve tool fixes landed this half (HDR warning, circle icons, wards, recall rule, K and F). The real match ID was scrubbed from one code comment and one test; it remains in branch history from 944b0dc (no force-push). Run data, plots and strips stay out of git. Report: REPORT-R2.md.

questions.text: (react) Run the short PC validation? About 30 min at your Windows PC on the same game as before: HDR off, minimap pass, one sign-out and sign-in, top-down window, re-mark the hand check, send to brain. It measures the R2 fixes, above all route A after the identity bug K.

chips.label: Tonight
chips.consequence: You run it tonight; the overseer scores it tomorrow and updates docs/scout-findings.md with the real post-fix numbers.

chips.label: This week
chips.consequence: You run it on a free evening this week; the merge and the route wait until then, and nothing else is blocked.

chips.label: Later — remind me
chips.consequence: Nothing runs now. The findings stay as written (route A on 57 frames only), and a later card reminds you.

questions.recommend: This week. It needs 30 calm minutes and one Windows sign-out, and nothing else waits on it.

questions.text: (react) Route for the Scout product round. The rule says B-first (A is not GO, B is). I recommend overriding it to A+B with B on key windows: B records only one window per Windows sign-in, so a whole game would take about seven sign-ins; A is the only full-game source, and its PARTIAL comes mostly from a bug that is now fixed. The validation run confirms or reverses this.

chips.label: A+B, B on key windows
chips.consequence: The product round tracks the whole game from the minimap and adds top-down windows for fights and objectives (about 4 min per game plus 30 s and a sign-in per window).

chips.label: B-first
chips.consequence: The product round builds on the top-down view (better accuracy) and needs a way around one recording per sign-in before it covers a whole game; the minimap only fills gaps.

chips.label: A-only
chips.consequence: The product round uses the minimap only: simplest, one pass of about 4 min per game, coarser positions (PARTIAL today), no top-down detail in fights.

questions.recommend: A+B, B on key windows. It is the only route that covers a whole game today and still uses B's accuracy where it matters.

questions.text: (react) Land tools/scout/ and docs/scout-findings.md on main? Nothing in src/ changes, and no run data is merged (runs, plots and strips are git-ignored). The findings are written but route A's numbers rest on 57 frames until the validation run.

chips.label: Yes, merge
chips.consequence: The overseer lands the branch after a fresh verifier's VERIFY-R2 says PASS; a later validation round lands as a small follow-up.

chips.label: Not yet — after validation
chips.consequence: The branch stays open; the validation run may change scorer or tracker code, and the findings and the merge go together after it.

questions.recommend: Not yet — after validation. The run may change scorer code, and merging once avoids landing numbers we already expect to replace.

questions.text: (react) Delete the quarantined wrong-monitor probe PNGs and the v1 run on brain? The PNGs show the wrong monitor (finding A) and are evidence of nothing. v1 is the only HDR-on run.

chips.label: Delete both
chips.consequence: The overseer deletes the quarantined PNGs and the whole v1 run; the HDR row in the findings keeps its numbers but can no longer be recomputed.

chips.label: Keep v1, delete PNGs
chips.consequence: The quarantined PNGs go; the v1 run stays local on brain as the HDR baseline until the product round, then is deleted.

chips.label: Keep all
chips.consequence: Nothing is deleted; the PNGs stay quarantined on brain.

questions.recommend: Keep v1, delete PNGs. The PNGs hold screens of the wrong monitor and serve nothing; v1 is the only HDR-on measurement and stays local.
